visual_goal: Show that interactive and batch traffic share the lookup service but not the queue, and that every cache miss passes one upstream budget broker that paces purchases and records spend.
prompt: A left-to-right architecture illustration. Top left: a generic dealer computer screen labeled 'Dealer screens'. Bottom left: a stack of job sheets labeled 'Client batch jobs'. Top row: one arrow from 'Dealer screens' right to a gate box labeled 'API gateway'. Bottom row: one arrow from 'Client batch jobs' right to a row of queued boxes labeled 'Batch lane queue'. One arrow from 'API gateway' down-right into a central box labeled 'Lookup service', and one arrow from 'Batch lane queue' up-right into the same 'Lookup service'. One arrow from 'Lookup service' right to a database cylinder labeled 'Specbook cache'. One orange arrow from 'Specbook cache' right to a valve-shaped box labeled 'Upstream budget broker', labeled 'miss'. One arrow from 'Upstream budget broker' right to a single generic supplier building with the label 'Paid providers' written once beneath it. One arrow from 'Upstream budget broker' down to a ledger book labeled 'Meterline'. Each of these nine quoted labels appears exactly once; no other words in the image.
alt: Dealer screens enter through the API gateway and client batch jobs through a batch lane queue paced by budget; both reach the lookup service and Specbook cache, and cache misses go through the upstream budget broker to paid providers, with spend per client recorded in Meterline.

visual_goal: Show the cost model joining five sources on shared tags and producing cost per call path, cost to serve and spend alerts.
prompt: A top-to-bottom funnel illustration. Top row: five small source cards side by side, labeled 'Usage events', 'Upstream cost events', 'Cloud billing export', 'Supplier invoices' and 'Support tickets'. Each card has one arrow down into a single central rounded box labeled 'Cost model'; the arrow from 'Supplier invoices' is labeled 'monthly reconciliation'. From 'Cost model' three arrows down to three output cards side by side: a small bar chart labeled 'Cost per call path', a shop-front icon labeled 'Cost to serve', and a bell icon labeled 'Spend alerts'. Icons carry no currency symbols; use plain coins, receipts and gears. These ten quoted labels are the only words in the image.
alt: Five sources, usage events, upstream cost events, cloud billing export, supplier invoices with monthly reconciliation and support tickets, feed a cost model that produces cost per call path, cost to serve and spend alerts.
